in_arabic.name: منصار
in_arabic.meaning: من يمنع و يدافع بكل قوة و شدة
in_arabic.long_meaning: منصار هو اسم علم مذكر من أصل عربي و معناه: من يمنع و يدافع بكل قوة و شدة، الشخص الذي يقوم بالدفاع عن الناس و يحميهم من المخاطر. و هو مشتق من جذر 'ن-ص-ر' الذي يعني النصرة و الدعم.

in_urdu.name: منصار
in_urdu.meaning: جو شخص طاقت کے ساتھ مدد اور دفاع کرتا ہے
in_urdu.long_meaning: منصار ایک مذکر نام ہے جو عربی زبان سے نکلا ہے۔ اس کا مطلب ہے جو شخص طاقت کے ساتھ مدد اور دفاع کرتا ہے، یعنی جو اپنے دفاع میں مضبوط ہوتا ہے اور دوسروں کی مدد کرنے کی طاقت رکھتا ہے۔ یہ نام عربی جڑ 'ن-ص-ر' سے ماخوذ ہے جس کا مطلب ہے مدد کرنا اور حمایت کرنا۔

in_hindi.name: मंसार
in_hindi.meaning: जो व्यक्ति शक्ति के साथ सहायता और रक्षा करता है
in_hindi.long_meaning: मंसार एक पुल्लिंग नाम है जो अरबी भाषा से लिया गया है। इसका अर्थ है जो व्यक्ति शक्ति के साथ सहायता और रक्षा करता है, यानी जो अपने रक्षा में मजबूत होता है और दूसरों की मदद करने की शक्ति रखता है। यह नाम अरबी मूल 'न-ص-र' से निकला है जिसका अर्थ है मदद करना और समर्थन करना।

in_pashto.name: منصار
in_pashto.meaning: هغه کسي چې په زوره دفاع او ملاتړ کوي
in_pashto.long_meaning: منصار د مذکر نوم دی چی د عربي ژبې څخه اخیستل شوی دی. دغه نوم معنی لري هغه کسي چې په زوره دفاع او ملاتړ کوي، يعنی هغه څوک چې په خپل دفاع کې قوي وي او د نورو سره د مرستې کولو طاقت لري. دا نوم د عربي ريښې 'ن-ص-ر' څخه اخیستل شوی دی چې معنی يې مرسته کول او حمايت کول دي.

in_english.name: Mansar
in_english.meaning: One who defends and supports with strength and power
in_english.long_meaning: Mansar is a masculine name of Arabic origin. It means one who defends and supports with strength and power. The name is derived from the Arabic root 'n-s-r' which signifies support, help, and defense. In Islamic tradition, the name Mansar embodies the qualities of courage, protection, and resilience. Historically, the name has been used in various Muslim cultures to denote individuals known for their bravery and strong sense of justice. The spiritual significance of the name Mansar lies in its connotation of safeguarding and upholding the rights of others.

data.cultural_impact: ** Al-Mansur's rule marked a turning point in Islamic history, as he brought about a renaissance of knowledge, arts, and sciences that lasted for several centuries. His patronage of intellectuals and scholars led to the translation of Greek and Syriac texts into Arabic, expanding the Islamic world's knowledge base and contributing significantly to the advancement of European intellectual thought.
data.spiritual_significance: ** As a caliph, Al-Mansur embodied the Islamic virtue of 'siyada' (helps others). His name 'Al-Mansur' emphasized the importance of providing aid and support to those in need, reflecting a fundamental aspect of Islamic teachings. This spiritual significance can be seen in the ongoing traditions of communal support and cooperation within Islamic communities, as well as the broader humanistic emphasis on assisting others in various aspects of life.

historical_references.reference: Mansar-i-Sabha, a mosque and mausoleum complex built by Sultan Mahmud Ghazni in Ghazni, Afghanistan, in 1030-1031 AD. It was the burial site for the sultan and is renowned for its architectural beauty and intricate decorations.

Mansurah, a fortress city built by Sultan Qutb-ud-din Aibak in 1206 AD near Delhi, India, in memory of Muhammad Ghori. The city was named after Mansurah, the name of the Prophet Muhammad's daughter, and served as the capital of the Delhi Sultanate.
